App.topicKa: How do I ask a question?
App.tutorWa: は is usually read “ha”, but as a topic particle it is pronounced “wa”. In 私は学生です (I am a student), は introduces 私 as the topic: “As for me…” The particle spelling preserves a historical reading.
App.tutorKa: For a basic polite question, put か at the end of a sentence: 学生です (I am a student) becomes 学生ですか (Are you a student?). Japanese often leaves out the subject when the context is clear.
App.tutorNo: の connects two nouns. It can show possession: 私の本 means “my book”. It can also describe a relationship: 日本語の先生 means “a Japanese-language teacher”. Read the whole phrase for context.
